errors_meaning: Per point: stat = statistical uncertainty (absolute, pb/GeV). syst = systematic uncertainty combined with luminosity uncertainty in quadrature (absolute); the paper's systematic column is asymmetric (+hi/-lo) and the larger leg was used as the symmetric magnitude before adding lumi in quadrature. total = stat (+) syst (+) lumi all in quadrature (absolute). errors_meaning: stat = statistical uncertainty (HEPData 'stat' symmetric component); syst = total systematic uncertainty = quadrature sum of ALL systematic components EXCLUDING the luminosity component (sysLumi, ~2.1% per bin, kept separate). total = sqrt(stat^2 + syst^2). This matches the paper's figure convention (outer error bars = stat+syst added in quadrature, excluding luminosity) and the 'exp.' uncertainty definition. Asymmetric systematic components were symmetrized using max(|plus|,|minus|) per component; the resulting +/- totals agree to better than 3% in every bin.

Each central value carries a 'stat' component and ~90 individual systematic NP components in HEPData; 'syst' here is their quadrature sum excluding the separately listed luminosity component (sysLumi). Internal checks: sysLumi/central = 2.100% for the first bin (matches integrated 8 pb / 399 pb), and sum(central x bin-width) = 114.5 pb for |eta|<0.6 (a sensible fraction of the full |eta|<2.37 fiducial sigma_meas = 399 +/- 13 (exp.) +/- 8 (lumi.) pb). errors_meaning: Eta-INTEGRATED dsigma/dET in pb/GeV. The source table (CMS PRL 106, 082001, arXiv:1012.0799, paper.tex Table tab:data_theory) natively prints the PER-UNIT-ETA double-differential d^2 sigma/(dET^gamma deta^gamma) in nb/GeV. To deliver the requested eta-integrated dsigma/dET in pb/GeV, every source value was multiplied by 2900 = delta_eta(2.9) * 1000(nb->pb). Per-point 'stat' = statistical uncertainty in pb/GeV (the +/- printed in the cross-section column, caption: 'Uncertainties in the cross sections are statistical', also scaled by 2900). Per-point 'syst' = total systematic in absolute pb/GeV computed as central * (larger-magnitude asymmetric percent)/100; the systematic is natively ASYMMETRIC and quoted in PERCENT in the table's third column (exact (+,-)% per bin in conversion_note). 'total' = sqrt(stat^2 + syst^2) in pb/GeV using the larger-magnitude syst. An additional overall 11% luminosity normalization uncertainty is NOT included in any field (kept separate per the paper).
source: arXiv:1012.0799 (CMS, PRL 106, 082001), file 'paper.tex', Table \label{tab:data_theory} (lines 286-319). Re-downloaded from https://arxiv.org/e-print/1012.0799 and re-read independently. Table header (rrcc): ET^gamma (GeV) | d^2 sigma/dET^gamma deta^gamma (nb/GeV) | Syst. Unc. (%) | U. Caption: 'Isolated prompt photon cross section for |eta^gamma|<1.45 and in bins of ET^gamma. Uncertainties in the cross sections are statistical. An additional 11% luminosity uncertainty is not included in the systematic uncertainty (third column). The last column reports the corrections for finite detector resolution.' Cross-section definition (line 216): d^2 sigma/dET^gamma deta^gamma = N^gamma/(L U eps DeltaET^gamma Deltaeta^gamma) with Deltaeta^gamma=2.9 (line 219). Macros (my-definitions.tex): etgamma=ET^gamma, etagamma=eta^gamma. Integrated luminosity 2.9 pb^-1 (line 26; numerically coincides with Deltaeta=2.9 but is a distinct quantity).
